subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Earthquake-Resistant Design: Building to Bend, Not Break
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Earthquake-Resistant Design: Building to Bend, Not Break.

hook.text: Japan's Yokohama Landmark Tower sways up to 2 feet in an earthquake. It's designed to bend because rigid buildings break.

buildup.text: Base isolation separates a building from the ground with rubber bearings. Earth shakes beneath while the building stays still.

discovery.text: Tuned mass dampers — massive pendulums inside skyscrapers — swing opposite to building motion, canceling out sway.

twist.text: Taipei 101's 730-ton damper is a tourist attraction. Visitors watch it swing during typhoons — it moved five feet in Soudelor.

climax.text: Shape-memory alloy joints deform in earthquakes and return to their original shape afterward. Self-centering buildings are coming.

punchline.text: Isolate the base. Damp the sway. Let it bend. Never let it break.

quiz.question: How do base isolation systems protect buildings during earthquakes?
options: They anchor the building deep into bedrock so it cannot move at all
Rubber bearings separate the building from the ground, letting the earth shake underneath
Springs at the base absorb seismic energy and convert it into electrical power
